description: Eliminated critical race conditions in the quote book logic by engineering a custom TCP socket server to emulate the NASDAQ SQF protocol, implementing manual packet framing and buffer management.
Achieved lock-free concurrency by replacing 4,000+ dictionaries with a transaction queue architecture, removing context-switching overhead and ensuring data consistency for high-frequency updates.

Enabled large-scale regression testing of 2,000+ live trading instances by designing a 'Safety Mode' system that audits full runtime configurations and captures state snapshots immediately prior to market connection.
Automated the build and deployment pipeline using TeamCity and Octopus Deploy, integrating the emulator into the daily testing suite to reduce manual QA cycle time by 80%.
Engineered an end-to-end monitoring and alerting solution (ASP.NET Core, Typescript) to secure and ensure uptime for 6,000+ critical production servers.
Designed a high-throughput distributed service to ingest and process over 1.25 million log entries per minute, streaming data into a partitioned MS SQL Server for anomaly detection.
Reduced deadlocks by >90% and tripled throughput by diagnosing Entity Framework's internal MERGE lock contention and refactoring the persistence layer to bypass unnecessary read-verifications.
Implemented a server-based sharding strategy for log ingestion, ensuring balanced load distribution across database partitions and preventing write-heavy hotspots during market open.
Mitigated resource leaks and security vulnerabilities by developing a Python and Robot Framework monitoring system to detect and alert on orphaned processes.
Restored high availability for core trading services by analyzing and resolving a persistent deadlock in a proprietary, low-latency C++ communication system.
Automated the analysis of process memory dumps to proactively identify memory leaks in long-running C++ trading processes before they caused critical OOM crashes.
Reverse-engineered Stanford's MOSS plagiarism detection algorithm, analyzing its string-matching and statistical techniques to identify vulnerabilities and inform development of a new tool.
Engineered a distributed data ingestion pipeline using Traefik and FastAPI to preprocess and queue massive volumes of source code submissions for algorithmic analysis.
Deployed the analysis engine via Docker containers, ensuring consistent execution environments across distributed compute nodes and enabling horizontal scaling.
